chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan ibn Yahya from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed Hajj al-Mufrad, then entered Mecca, circled the Kaaba, and performed Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwah. He said: 'He should exit the state of Ihram and make it Umrat al-Mut'ah, unless he brought the sacrificial animal (Hady), in which case he cannot exit Ihram until the sacrificial animal reaches its place of sacrifice.'

key_terms.حَجّ مُفْرِد: Hajj al-Mufrad: A form of Hajj where the pilgrim enters Ihram with the intention of Hajj only, without combining it with Umrah.
key_terms.سَاقَ الْهَدْيَ: Saqa al-Hady: To bring along the sacrificial animal for the Hajj.
key_terms.سَعَى: Sa'i: The ritual walking between the hills of Safa and Marwah.
key_terms.طَافَ بِالْبَيْتِ: Tawaf: The ritual circumambulation of the Kaaba.
key_terms.مَحِلَّهُ: Mahillahu: The place where the sacrificial animal is to be slaughtered.
key_terms.مُتْعَةً: Mut'ah: Referring to Umrat al-Mut'ah (Umrah of Convenience), performed after Hajj to complete the pilgrimage obligations.
key_terms.يُحِلَّ: Yuhill: To exit the state of Ihram (ritual consecration).

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a Mufrid pilgrim who performs Umrah rites before exiting Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the procedural distinction between Hajj al-Mufrad and Hajj al-Qiran, specifically addressing the scenario where a pilgrim performs Umrah rites before completing the Hajj obligations. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that unless the pilgrim has already brought the sacrificial animal (Hady) required for Qiran, he must exit Ihram after Umrah and re-enter for Hajj as a separate act, thereby avoiding the penalty of remaining in Ihram until the Hady arrives. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the distinct validity of Umrah and Hajj when performed separately, contrasting with the Hanafi view which often treats them as a single combined unit in this context.
